atalaya.title: Atalaya
atalaya.tagline: Different sources, one list with clear criteria
atalaya.summary: Atalaya is a Python CLI that pulls roles from several sources, removes duplicates, scores them against a profile and prepares a cover-letter draft for review.
problem: Atalaya started because looking for remote work means repeating the same searches. Each source publishes differently, and the same role can appear more than once.
The CLI gathers the results, stops duplicates and puts the roles that fit the profile first. The person still decides which application is worth pursuing.

decisions.title: Each source has its own reader
decisions.body: The readers live separately and have their own tests. If a source changes its format, the failure stays contained and the others keep delivering roles.

decisions.title: The scoring weights are written down
decisions.body: Stack 0.50 · remote 0.25 · seniority 0.15 · language 0.10, with the stack compared by Jaccard plus a bonus when it touches the core of the profile. When a role scores high you can see why, instead of trusting a number from nowhere.

decisions.title: Duplicates are stopped by the database
decisions.body: The URL is UNIQUE in SQLite. If the application logic slips, the duplicate still doesn't get in.

decisions.title: Drafting sits behind an adapter
decisions.body: The CLI and SDK expose the same function. The rest of the program requests a draft without depending on one specific way to generate it.

decisions.title: Nothing is marked as sent unless you say so
decisions.body: For roles that only take a web form, the CLI copies the letter and opens the browser. Recording the application means running it again with the flag set by hand.

atalaya.note: Strict typing with mypy and a strict linter. Python 3.12, Typer, httpx, SQLite.

savemymoneynow.title: SaveMyMoneyNow
savemymoneynow.tagline: Import statements without tying the product to one template
savemymoneynow.summary: SaveMyMoneyNow turns statements into a spending dashboard. It finds the header row, proposes a column mapping and waits for the user to confirm before importing.
problem: SaveMyMoneyNow receives spreadsheets where the header can appear after several information rows. Column names, dates and decimal formats also change between files.
A dedicated reader for each layout would mean maintaining the same logic several times. The wizard looks for the file structure and lets the user correct its proposal.

decisions.title: The header is detected from its content
decisions.body: A wizard scores the first rows, keeps the one that looks like the header and proposes which column is Date, which is Description and which is Amount, reading both the name and what sits underneath. You confirm or correct.

decisions.title: The duplicate fingerprint leaves the amount out
decisions.body: The fingerprint uses date and description. This keeps a purchase corrected after a partial refund from becoming a new movement when the month is imported again. The amount stays separate for auditing.

decisions.title: Import batches expire on their own
decisions.body: What the wizard produces lives two days and Mongo deletes it; the final movements never expire. Picking the wizard back up too late returns a 410 with its explanation, rather than working on half-finished data.

decisions.title: The PDF has a cap and the spreadsheet doesn't
decisions.body: PDF exports accept up to five thousand rows because the library builds the whole document in memory. Spreadsheet exports write as they go and can handle larger histories.

decisions.title: The tests build the statements they are going to read
decisions.body: They spin up Mongo in memory and build statements with different layouts during the test. Each case declares the structure it expects to read.

savemymoneynow.note: React, Node, Express and MongoDB. Tests with Vitest and in-memory Mongo.

strev.title: Strev
strev.tagline: Trainer management with sensitive data and asynchronous work
strev.summary: Strev is a web product for personal trainers. It brings together daily management, payments and video technique analysis without making the interface wait for the model.
problem: Strev handles routines, progress and health data that need specific protection inside the application.
Video technique analysis takes longer than a normal request. The interface needs to respond while that work continues in the background.

decisions.title: Sensitive fields are encrypted separately
decisions.body: The rest of the document remains available for normal queries while health data stays protected inside the database.

decisions.title: Video goes to a queue
decisions.body: The request returns straight away and the analysis runs elsewhere. The model is Gemini and the job is judging exercise technique, not generating routines.

decisions.title: If Redis goes down, the API holds
decisions.body: The rate limiter degrades when the cache is unavailable and lets the main service keep responding.

decisions.title: Every download checks ownership
decisions.body: The application checks who requested the video before issuing a temporary download URL.

decisions.title: Maintenance starts in preview mode
decisions.body: Purge, migration and encryption tasks first show what they would change. Destructive execution requires an explicit command.

strev.note: React, Node, Express, MongoDB, Redis with BullMQ, Stripe and Gemini. Closed source.

sereno.title: Sereno
sereno.tagline: See which session is working, waiting or stuck
sereno.summary: Sereno is a single-file Python terminal UI that reads the local histories of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Antigravity. It separates sessions that are writing, running a command, waiting for a reply or already stopped, without sending data off the machine.
problem: Sereno started with the problem of following several agent sessions at once. A live process does not tell you whether it is writing, inside a command, waiting for a reply or stopped.
The four CLIs record their activity in different formats. Sereno reads those local histories and returns comparable states without copying real prompts or depending on a remote service.

decisions.title: Histories stay where the tools wrote them
decisions.body: Sereno reads the local transcript queues of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Antigravity. Each reader maps its format to the same states without uploading the content elsewhere.

decisions.title: The last useful event determines the state
decisions.body: A tool_use without its tool_result means the session is in a command. The stop_reason and later events separate writing, waiting and stopped.

decisions.title: The cache follows mtime
decisions.body: A transcript is only parsed again when its modification time changes. Refreshing stays cheap even with many sessions open.

decisions.title: No networking is enforced by a test
decisions.body: The application opens no connections. An AST test rejects imports from networking modules, so that guarantee does not rely on someone remembering a rule while editing the file.

decisions.title: The demo never touches real sessions
decisions.body: Demo mode uses synthetic histories in an isolated environment. The public capture shows the states without client names, prompts or machine data.

sereno.note: macOS and Linux. Python 3.8+, curses and tmux. MIT licence. The demo uses synthetic data.
